page: Microsoft Azure D96pls_v6 is a Dplsv6-series virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM64 architecture with Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processors clocked at 3.4 GHz. The CPU configuration provides one thread per core, meaning hyperthreading is not active. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the middle 50%. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, registering top-tier results for both small-block cached and large-block uncached read-only memory bandwidth, as well as large-block write bandwidth.

Due to its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server represents a compute-focused hardware profile that offers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. Top-tier benchmark results in Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and software compilation with Clang make it highly suitable for web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and database operations. It also demonstrates strong to top-tier performance in medium-to-large LLM text generation tasks despite the lack of a dedicated GPU.
